data.body:
RCA (Phase 1 complete) — root cause PROVEN, deterministic, and NOT load-related.

## Root cause (one changeable artifact)

src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/access_check.py:14 binds the class by value —
`from rebar_reconciler.adapters.jira.acli import AcliClient` — and :99 freezes that
binding into a default expression: `def run_access_check(*, env=None, client_cls=AcliClient, ...)`.
A default expression is evaluated ONCE, at module import.

The test patches the seam on the DEFINING module, not the consumer:
`monkeypatch.setattr(acli, "AcliClient", FakeClient)`
(tests/interfaces/facades/test_bridge_programmatic_e2e_heldout.py:210).

`rebar.bridge_check_access()` reaches the module via `_lib_ops._engine_module()`, which ends in
`importlib.import_module(...)` (src/rebar/_lib_ops.py:186) — i.e. it returns the sys.modules
CACHE if the module was already imported.

So the patch reaches the code under test ONLY when `rebar_reconciler.access_check` has not yet
been imported at patch time: the fresh import then reads the already-patched attribute and
`client_cls` defaults to FakeClient. If ANY earlier test in the process already imported
access_check, the module is cached with the REAL AcliClient frozen into the default, the
monkeypatch is invisible, the probe constructs a REAL Jira client, STEP_CREATE raises, and the
verdict is FAIL. The test's oracle never sees the fake.

Named polluter in the full suite: tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_preflight_project_visibility.py
imports access_check, and tests/unit runs before tests/interfaces. Within tests/interfaces alone
the only other importer is facades/test_bridge_vocabulary_e2e_heldout.py, and "programmatic"
sorts BEFORE "vocabulary" — which is exactly why the tier passes in isolation.

## Proof — discriminating experiments (all on THIS host, quiet and saturated)

1. Deterministic repro, 6/6, two files only, no full suite, ~10s:
   `pytest tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_preflight_project_visibility.py \
           tests/interfaces/facades/test_bridge_programmatic_e2e_heldout.py -q -p no:randomly`
   -> 1 failed, 19 passed. Same `assert 'FAIL' == 'PASS'`.
2. Control, target file alone, 3/3: 4 passed.
3. THE DISCRIMINATOR — same two files, same host, same load, ONLY the order reversed
   (target first, polluter second): 20 passed. Co-presence is not the variable; IMPORT ORDER is.
4. Runtime oracle (scratch probe, both branches observed executing):
   - polluted: access_check.AcliClient -> <class '...acli.AcliClient'>; default client_cls ->
     the REAL AcliClient; acli.AcliClient -> FakeClient. verdict FAIL, and the probe made a LIVE
     call: STEP_CREATE reason=exception detail="Issue DIG-5924 not found".
   - clean: access_check.AcliClient -> FakeClient; default client_cls -> FakeClient; verdict PASS,
     all six steps.

## The load confound is BROKEN — hypothesis 2 is rejected

Both prior observations were full-suite runs on a saturated host, so load and suite-breadth were
confounded. Controlled directly: `pytest tests/interfaces/facades` (577 tests incl. the target)
run under DELIBERATE host saturation (24 spinners, load average 43-48) -> 576 passed, 1 skipped,
0 failed, in 546s vs ~5s quiet — a ~100x slowdown with ZERO failures. Conversely the two-file
repro fails in ~10s on a quiet host. Load is neither necessary nor sufficient; import order is
both. "Test-ordering dependence in general" (hyp. 3) is also refined out: reversing the order of
the SAME two files flips the result, so it is not xdist/tmp-path/seed — it is one named seam.

## Second symptom, same single cause

In the polluted order this `pytestmark = pytest.mark.unit` test performs REAL network I/O against
a live Jira. That is not a separate defect; it is the same frozen default.

## Attribution — caused_by f789-3f9d-8b35-4e0d (uncheered-sombre-bumblebee), class: OMISSION

`git blame -w -C -M -L 99,99` and `git log -L 99,99` both terminate at fa1bf13845
(2026-08-10, "Expose bridge operations through library and MCP", rebar-ticket: f789-3f9d-8b35-4e0d).
`git show --stat fa1bf13845` confirms that commit CREATED both access_check.py (+156) and
test_bridge_programmatic_e2e_heldout.py (+236). The seam and the test that cannot reliably reach
it shipped in the same change; the test was green at authoring only by import-order luck.

This is an OMISSION, not a regression: the isolation was never established. Nothing broke it —
`git log -L 99,99` shows the line has never been modified. The date test agrees: the implicated
line dates 2026-08-10 and the first observation (session log skeletal-soaplike-caracal) is
2026-08-16, with no good->bad transition in between.

Divergence from the default: a whole-file blame majority would name a much later toucher
(1e9078f47a 2026-08-18 or 40b8ac8295 2026-08-18, both unrelated refactors). Line-scoped blame
names f789. I am attributing to f789.

Contributing factor, deliberately NOT the origin: ticket 5ea3-76e5-480a-4464 (3182cd470a,
2026-08-13) fixed the IDENTICAL construct two lines below — `sleep_fn=time.sleep` ->
`sleep_fn=_retry_sleep` — and documented the invariant in the `_retry_sleep` docstring
(access_check.py:44-58), but did not sweep the `client_cls=AcliClient` sibling directly above it.
That is a missed Step-7 construct sweep, not the introduction; the defect predates it by 3 days.

## Legitimacy: defect (cited)

The `_retry_sleep` docstring at access_check.py:44-58 is an in-file, deliberate design invariant
for this exact module: injection seams must resolve at CALL time so that "whether a test's patch
reached this" does not depend on "whether this module happened to be imported first", while
"production behaviour is byte-identical". `client_cls=AcliClient` violates that stated invariant.

## Fix direction (Phase 2)

Restore the documented invariant at the seam: resolve AcliClient at call time, mirroring
`_retry_sleep`. Production behaviour byte-identical (still AcliClient); only the resolution
moment changes. Explicitly NOT doing: weakening the assertion, adding a retry/sleep, xfail/flaky
marks, or widening any behaviour.
